description.p: Northstar Web Browser is a clean-room web browser written from scratch in C, with a GTK 4 user interface and a libcurl network stack. It is built to be small, secure, and readable by a single person end to end.

ul.li: A from-scratch HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript engine — no forked browser engine.
One page per window and one process: the page engine runs in the shell process, behind a seccomp + Landlock sandbox on Linux.
No JIT, which keeps the JavaScript attack surface small.
No telemetry: it does not phone home and does not track the user.

screenshot.caption: Northstar Web Browser showing a Wikipedia article

ul.li: Dragging with the mouse ends where the button is released, so chess.com pieces can be dragged, and chess.com guests are paired with an opponent again.
BankID sign-in works: sessionStorage lasts for the window, and unknown Content-Encoding values no longer fail the request.
Cloudflare Turnstile no longer fails, as shadow roots stay out of light-DOM walks and cross-origin messages keep their source.
Function.prototype.caller works for sloppy-mode functions, fixing freecivweb.com singleplayer games.
Local files the Linux sandbox will not open get an error page that explains why.
Settings, History and Page Source open again from the menu, the keyboard shortcuts and the address bar.
Pages that walk window.frames no longer hang, nested CSS math functions resolve rem against the root font size, and up to 64 sounds can be loaded at once.
QuickJS builds no longer fail when Bellard's qjs is installed.
Northstar can be installed from npm as northstar-browser.
Fixes for a heap overflow in the HTML tokenizer, a use-after-free in JavaScript modules, and a crash when a page and a frame share a stylesheet.
Safe Browsing now checks redirect hops and form POSTs, HSTS entries expire when their max-age ends, and linked stylesheets are checked against their Subresource Integrity hash.
Deeply nested intrinsic-size layouts and select.add() cycles no longer hang the page.
localStorage keeps keys with special characters, CSS animations run at the full frame rate on 60 Hz displays, and the window keeps following the desktop theme.
An Arch Linux package is available.
The browser is renamed Northstar Web Browser; the executable, settings and profiles carry over unchanged.
Text layout is vendored in the source tree, so offline and distribution builds no longer fetch it, and CJK text sits on the same baseline as the text around it.
The browser starts again on NVIDIA's proprietary driver under X11.
open-internet-browser is installed as a second name for the browser.
Eleven crash fixes for pages that modify the DOM or prototypes while the engine is working on them, and for malformed SVG path data.
Client hints report Northstar instead of Chrome, and error messages, stack traces and built-in functions look like the engine the user agent names, for sites that compare the two.
The Linux sandbox no longer exposes the home directory on LightDM sessions and refuses executable memory wherever page content runs.
Local HTML files can no longer read other local files through frames or canvases.
document.cookie follows cookies set by fetch() and XMLHttpRequest responses.
Memory-safety fixes in the media demuxers, canvas, WebAssembly and audio code, and about 3,800 lines of unused code removed.

description.p: Streaming video, performance and security release.

ul.li: Video plays Media Source Extensions streams and ordinary MP4 and WebM files (AV1, VP9, H.264 with AAC or Opus), decoded on a thread of its own.
Restyling, relayout and painting after page changes do much less work, and large scripts compile in the background.
JavaScript passes every test262 test quickjs-ng enables.
A source-wide security review fixed several memory-safety and cross-origin issues.
Positioned, inline, grid and table layout, iframes and the address bar follow the standards more closely.
MPEG-1 video decodes as it plays, plays its sound and shows working playback controls.
WebAssembly runs on a faster interpreter, still without a JIT.
A source-wide security audit fixed several memory-safety issues.
Grid, inline and positioned layout, hit-testing and frame messaging are more standards-conformant.
Closing the window no longer crashes, and 32-bit Linux builds are supported.
Deeply nested pages and deeply recursive scripts no longer crash the browser on macOS and musl.
Frames get their own window events, document lifecycle, origin, focus and name.
postMessage, MessageChannel and structured cloning follow the HTML standard across windows, frames and workers.
Events, built-in objects and engine-implemented functions look as they do in other browsers.
Northstar can optionally be built on Fabrice Bellard's original QuickJS.
The Microsoft Store package is built under the Northstar Browser product identity.
audio and video are real HTMLMediaElements driven by the in-process mixer and the MPEG-1 frame timeline.
Only changed regions are repainted, scrolling shifts the previous frame, and text measurements and blurred box shadows are cached across relayouts.
Every WHATWG Encoding Standard encoding is decoded and encoded in-tree, for pages, TextDecoder, XMLHttpRequest, links and form submissions.
WebCrypto gains Ed448 and X448 and follows the specification's algorithm normalization; structuredClone and Blob follow their specifications.
Cross-origin frames and images are isolated more strictly, and every subresource request passes a single policy check.
dialog, popover, invoker commands, autofocus, image maps and srcset follow the HTML standard.
Grid, table, flexbox, float, cascade and align-content layout fixes, and textareas sized by CSS height.
Entering full screen shows a five-second notice naming the host, and Element.requestFullscreen() rejects as the Fullscreen API specifies instead of pretending to succeed.
The address bar suggests matching bookmarks, ranked history entries and a search as you type.
The navigation toolbar is laid out like Mozilla 1.0 with icon-over-label buttons, and the about:start splash is redrawn.
The JavaScript engine is quickjs-ng v0.17.0; canvases are origin-tainted, cross-origin frames no longer expose their DOM, and postMessage matches targetOrigin exactly.
Downloads and clipboard writes require a recent user gesture, subresource redirects keep their initiator, and the Linux sandbox probes the Landlock ABI at startup.
SVG, XML entity and CSS parsing are bounded; custom properties, color-mix(), shorthands and math functions follow their specifications.
Grid auto-placement is uncapped, floats and margin collapsing are placed per specification, and table column counting accounts for spanned cells.
Transitions and animations run on every property, backed by a Web Animations surface: Element.animate(), getAnimations(), and the animation and transition events follow the phase model.
border-image is implemented, and transform, the individual transform properties, gradients, background layers and box-shadow are validated and serialised the way their specifications say.
Flex layout resolves flexible lengths per css-flexbox-1 §9.7, column containers wrap, and grid items honour self-alignment, rtl track order and repeat(auto-fit).
Form constraint validation, stepUp/stepDown, showPicker() and label association follow the HTML specification; the last selected option of a select wins.
Selection highlights, copies and reports the text it is actually on, and double- and triple-click select a word or a block.
JavaScript can be turned off from the menu, view-source: shows a page's markup, and window.open no longer opens pop-ups without a click.
Fixed a use-after-free in MutationObserver delivery and another in the session URL, a hang in the CSS parser, and a read past the end of a linked stylesheet.
The browser prints: Ctrl+P lays the page out for paper and hands the sheets to the system print dialog, with @media print, @page and the break properties deciding where a sheet ends.
offsetLeft and offsetTop are measured from the offsetParent, which is what CSSOM View asks for and what most layout tests compare against.
CSS Scroll Snap moves a scroll container onto the nearest snap position, from the wheel and from scrollTop/scrollLeft.
Absolutely positioned flex children are placed by justify-content and align-self, and flex-wrap: wrap-reverse puts the first line last.
A frame reaches its parent: postMessage is delivered to the top window's listeners, each framed document is governed by its own Content-Security-Policy, and fetch() resolves with a real Response.
A paragraph measures the same whether or not another paragraph shaped its words first, because the font now decides where a shaped run may be cut.
Dynamic :has() selectors update after class, attribute and child-list mutations.
Percentage and elliptical border-radius resolve against the border box, so circular avatars are round.
Relative colour syntax, the color() function and one shared parser for all six colour functions.
Text is itemized, shaped and broken by ns-pango, which caches finished glyph strings across layouts.
The DOM insertion methods run the insertion steps, and getComputedStyle resolves every property it enumerates.
SVG is rendered by the engine instead of librsvg, so page stylesheets reach inside inline icons.
<video> plays MPEG-1, decoded in-tree, and responds to play, pause, currentTime, duration and readyState.
Animated PNG plays, and lossy WebP decodes through the memory-safe path.
gdk-pixbuf no longer decodes page images, so the set of decoders reachable from a web page is fixed at build time.
Square borders are painted inside the border box rather than centred on its edge.
Fixed an out-of-bounds read in the vendored MPEG-1 decoder, found by fuzzing.

description.p: Debian packaging and portability release, adding Debian 13 and sid CI builds.
Stability release fixing two memory-corruption bugs found with AddressSanitizer on live sites.

ul.li: Fixed a use-after-free when a page dropped its IntersectionObserver while the observer callback was running.
Fixed JS class-ID collisions between page sessions that ran the wrong finalizer on the wrong object, causing random crashes after navigating.
Dropdown (select) controls render their chosen option again, and native checkboxes no longer draw doubled with author CSS decorations.
Fixed a heap-corruption crash when closing the browser after using the bookmarks popover.
Updated the vendored Wuffs image decoders and the WAMR WebAssembly interpreter (CVE-2026-54913 loader fix).
New about:start splash artwork; refreshed Debian/RPM packaging; new Alpine (musl) and macOS CI builds.

description.p: Initial release of the Northstar GPL edition: a single-window, single-process desktop browser for Linux and Windows.
